biotools.summary: Morpheus is an open-source modeling and simulation framework for multi-scale and multicellular biological systems. The GUI allows to construct and simulate models from gene regulation, metabolism and signaling to tissue morphogenesis and their multi-scale feedbacks without the need to program. Morpheus is based on declarative modeling in biological terms and mathematical expressions and internally uses the domain-specific language MorpheusML, allowing for rapid model prototyping without extra code-compilation. Morpheus supports cell-based model formalisms, ODEs, PDEs, rule-based models, SBML models etc. (all freely coupled) as well as image-based modeling. It renders results in customizable 2D and 3D images or movies and offers analysis tools to extract features right during simulation. The plugin architecture makes it extensible. Binary installers are available for all major OS from the Morpheus homepage together with online courses, a public model repository and many more resources.

function.note: Morpheus allows to construct and simulate models from gene regulation, metabolism and signaling to tissue morphogenesis and their multi-scale feedbacks. Output data are configurations of all simulated cells and their state variables (as well as PDE fields, PDE fields on membranes of cells etc.) at all simulated time points. These output data can be stored in various text, image or movie formats as well as xml to be used as initial condition for a follow-up simulation. In-built analysis plugins allow to extract trajectory data [x,y,z](time) of moving cells, as one example.

Pathway or network models may be imported from SBML or MorpheusML files or manually defined in the GUI's model editor, then a model graph is generated that can interactively be filtered or pruned and exported in image file formats incl. SVG.

metadata.abstract: Summary: Morpheus is a modeling environment for the simulation and integration of cell-based models with ordinary differential equations and reaction-diffusion systems. It allows rapid development of multiscale models in biological terms and mathematical expressions rather than programming code. Its graphical user interface supports the entire workflow from model construction and simulation to visualization, archiving and batch processing. © The Author 2013. Published by Oxford University Press.
